metadata.title: Sensitivity of BioEmu Stability Benchmark Estimates to Sequential Post-hoc Structural Filtering
metadata.description:
This technical note examines the sensitivity of predicted protein stability estimates to sequential post-hoc structural filtering in a fixed BioEmu benchmark archive.

The analysis includes 154 systems (42 wild-type and 112 mutant systems) and 112 matched mutant–wild-type comparisons. The saved ensemble contained 302,800 frames. Official geometry filtering retained 298,188 frames, followed by an additional fixed peptide-ω screen retaining 272,381 frames.

Absolute changes in predicted ΔΔG of at least 0.1 kcal/mol occurred in 19 of 112 comparisons after geometry filtering and 40 of 112 comparisons after peptide-ω filtering, with 12 comparisons shared between these groups. The corresponding descriptive mean absolute errors against the benchmark experimental references were 0.702595, 0.696142, and 0.707681 kcal/mol across the three sequential ensembles.

System-level foldedness, predicted ΔG, matched ΔΔG, and cross-stage comparisons reveal how changes in retained conformations can be amplified or cancelled through shared wild-type references. These results document sensitivity of a fixed estimator to the selected structural subsets; they do not demonstrate a general improvement in predictive accuracy or recovery of equilibrium conformational populations.

The record contains a Technical Note, Supplementary Information, fixed-archive results, analysis and verification code, and provenance documentation. The scientific conclusions are limited to the archived inputs and specified filtering conditions.

Source repository : https://github.com/shomiyazaki-ai/bioemu-filter-sensitivity-ntbe-x2-omega
